```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

.opt_width  <- options(width = 120)
hook_output <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
flag_eval   <- vmTools:::dir_supports_links(tempdir())

knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  if (!is.null(n <- options$out.lines)) {
    x <- vmTools:::split_line_breaks(x)
    if (length(x) > n) x <- c(head(x, n %/% 2), "....", tail(x, n %/% 2 + 1))
    x <- paste(x, collapse = "\n")
  }
  hook_output(x, options)
})
```

```{r windows_note, echo = FALSE}
if (!flag_eval) {
  knitr::asis_output(
    "> **Note:** This machine cannot create symlinks (shortcuts) in its temp folder
    > (on Windows that needs a local disk). Code is shown but not evaluated on this system."
  )
}
```

```{r helpers, include = FALSE}
library(vmTools)
library(data.table)

print_tree <- function(x, level = Inf) vmTools:::dir_tree(x, level = level)

next_version <- function(root, date) {
  existing <- grep(
    sprintf("^%s\\.\\d{2}$", date),
    list.files(root), value = TRUE
  )
  idx <- if (length(existing) == 0) 0L else
    max(as.integer(sub(".*\\.", "", existing)))
  sprintf("%s.%02d", date, idx + 1L)
}

show_vars <- c("log_id", "timestamp", "version_name", "action", "comment")
```

This vignette assumes you've read the **Quick Start** guide and covers:

1. The Symlink Composer (`SLC`) for cross-project queries
2. Multiple roots per tool instance
3. Custom symlink types via the plugin architecture
4. Reports and discrepancy detection

Each section is self-contained — run them independently or in order.

---

# 1 — Symlink Composer (`SLC`)

When a production deliverable is assembled from several independent modeling pipelines — say, separate submodels for different geographic regions — each pipeline has its own SLT.  The **Symlink Composer** (`SLC`) lets you query across all of them at once: _"what is the current `best` set?"_

Think of each pipeline as an **instrument** in an orchestra.  Each instrument practises independently and keeps its own sheet music (SLT logs).  The **composer** (SLC) runs in 'read only' mode — it looks across all its instruments to discover "is every instrument ready for the final concert?"

## Setup: three independent sub-model pipelines

Each region has been worked on at different paces, so their `best` versions are on different dates.

```{r slc_setup, eval = flag_eval}
base_slc <- file.path(tempdir(), "slt_tech", "composer")

# Each region gets its own output root and SLT
regions <- c("north", "central", "south")

tools <- lapply(setNames(regions, regions), function(r) {
  root <- file.path(base_slc, r)
  dir.create(root, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  SLT$new(
    root_list        = setNames(list(root), r),
    central_log_root = root
  )
})
```

```{r slc_reset_cores, include = FALSE}
.opt_mc2 <- options(mc.cores = 1L)
```

Run each pipeline independently — different dates reflect real-world asynchronous development.

```{r slc_runs, eval = flag_eval}
run_dates <- c(north = "2024_09_01", central = "2024_09_08", south = "2024_09_15")

for (r in regions) {
  root <- file.path(base_slc, r)
  ver  <- next_version(root, run_dates[[r]])
  tools[[r]]$make_new_version_folder(version_name = ver)
  tools[[r]]$mark_best(version_name = ver, user_entry = list(comment = paste(r, "initial run")))
}
```

## Compose the set

```{r slc_compose, eval = flag_eval}
composer <- SLC$new(tool_list = tools)
composer$list_tools()
```

## Query the full `best` set

```{r slc_best, eval = flag_eval}
composer$roundup_all("best")
```

One table, every sub-model's current `best` — a single view of the full production-ready set, spanning three different run dates.

## Query `keep` or any other type

Querying a full `best` or `latest` set is probably most common, but _any_ symlink type set can be 'composed' across all its instruments.

```{r slc_keep_setup, eval = flag_eval}
# Archive the north run — it's being cited in a journal submission
north_best <- composer$roundup_all("best")[tool_name == "north", version_name]
tools$north$mark_keep(
  version_name = north_best,
  user_entry   = list(comment = "Journal submission 2024")
)

composer$roundup_all("keep")
```

## Find unmarked folders across every pipeline

```{r slc_unmarked, eval = flag_eval}
composer$roundup_all_unmarked()
```

```{r slc_cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = flag_eval}
unlink(base_slc, recursive = TRUE)
```

---

# 2 — Multiple Roots

A single SLT instance can manage several root directories at once.  This is useful when one pipeline run produces outputs that land in different locations — e.g. pre-model inputs and post-model results — but you want them versioned in lockstep under the same `version_name`.

## Setup

```{r multi_setup, eval = flag_eval}
base <- file.path(tempdir(), "slt_tech", "multi_root")

root_input  <- file.path(base, "to_model")
root_output <- file.path(base, "modeled")
dir.create(root_input,  recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(root_output, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

slt <- SLT$new(
  root_list = list(
    input  = root_input,
    output = root_output
  ),
  central_log_root = base
)
```

```{r multi_reset_cores, include = FALSE}
.opt_mc <- options(mc.cores = 1L)
```

Two roots, one tool.  Every `mark` or `make_new_version_folder` call operates on both roots in parallel.

## Create and mark

```{r multi_create, eval = flag_eval}
v1 <- next_version(root_input, "2024_06_01")
slt$make_new_version_folder(version_name = v1)

# Populate with dummy files
invisible(file.create(file.path(root_input,  v1, "prep.csv")))
invisible(file.create(file.path(root_output, v1, "results.csv")))

v2 <- next_version(root_input, "2024_06_01")
slt$make_new_version_folder(version_name = v2)
invisible(file.create(file.path(root_input,  v2, "prep.csv")))
invisible(file.create(file.path(root_output, v2, "results.csv")))

slt$mark_best(version_name = v1, user_entry = list(comment = "Initial run"))
```

```{r multi_tree, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(base, level = 2)
```

The `best` symlink appears in _both_ roots, pointing to v1 in each.  Promoting v2 demotes v1 everywhere at once.

```{r multi_promote, eval = flag_eval}
suppressMessages(
  slt$mark_best(version_name = v2, user_entry = list(comment = "Revised covariates"))
)
print_tree(base, level = 1)
```

```{r multi_cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = flag_eval}
unlink(base, recursive = TRUE)
```

---

# 3 — Custom Symlink Types (Plugin Architecture)

The four built-in types — `best`, `latest`, `keep`, `remove` — cover most workflows.  But the registry is extensible: call `new_symlink_type()` to define your own, then use the generic `$mark()` and `$roundup()` methods.

## Example: regulatory `hold` for clinical trials

In clinical-trial data pipelines, a regulatory agency can issue a **clinical hold** — an order to freeze a dataset in place pending review.  No one may delete, overwrite, or re-process that data until the hold is lifted.  This is different from `keep` (an internal convenience) because a `hold` has legal weight and should be immediately visible to anyone browsing the output directory.

### Register the type

```{r hold_register, eval = flag_eval}
new_symlink_type("hold", is_singleton = FALSE)
get_symlink_registry()[["hold"]]
```

`is_singleton = FALSE` because multiple datasets can be under hold simultaneously (each for a different regulatory inquiry).

- By contrast, `best` is a singleton type — only one folder can hold it at a time.
- Users may create singleton symlinks as well.
- Users may create as many new symlink types as they like.

### Use it

```{r hold_setup, eval = flag_eval}
base_hold <- file.path(tempdir(), "slt_tech", "trial_outputs")
dir.create(base_hold, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

slt_trial <- SLT$new(
  root_list        = list(trial = base_hold),
  central_log_root = base_hold
)
```

```{r hold_reset_cores, include = FALSE}
.opt_mc3 <- options(mc.cores = 1L)
```

```{r hold_create, eval = flag_eval}
# Simulate three analysis runs
for (i in 1:3) {
  ver <- next_version(base_hold, "2025_01_10")
  slt_trial$make_new_version_folder(version_name = ver)
}

# Mark run .02 with a regulatory hold
slt_trial$mark("hold", version_name = "2025_01_10.02",
               user_entry = list(comment = "FDA clinical hold — trial xxxx"))
```

```{r hold_tree, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(base_hold, level = 1)
```

The `hold_2025_01_10.02` symlink is now visible on the filesystem — any team member who `ls`es the directory sees it immediately.

### Roundup held datasets

```{r hold_roundup, eval = flag_eval}
slt_trial$roundup("hold")
```

When the hold is lifted, demote with `unmark()`:

```{r hold_unmark, eval = flag_eval}
slt_trial$unmark(version_name = "2025_01_10.02",
                 user_entry = list(comment = "Hold lifted — FDA clearance 2025-03-01"))
```

```{r hold_tree_after, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(base_hold, level = 1)
```

The audit trail lives in the versioned folder's log — when the hold was placed, by whom, and when it was released.

```{r hold_log, eval = flag_eval}
data.table::fread(
  file.path(base_hold, "2025_01_10.02", "logs", "log_version_history.csv")
)[, ..show_vars]
```

```{r hold_cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = flag_eval}
unlink(base_hold, recursive = TRUE)
```

# 4 — Reports and Discrepancy Detection

SLT auto-generates a `report_key_versions.csv` on every `mark` call.  Additional reports are available via `$make_reports()`.

## Setup

```{r rpt_setup, eval = flag_eval}
base_rpt <- file.path(tempdir(), "slt_tech", "reports")
dir.create(base_rpt, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

slt_rpt <- SLT$new(
  root_list        = list(output = base_rpt),
  central_log_root = base_rpt
)
```

```{r rpt_reset_cores, include = FALSE}
.opt_mc4 <- options(mc.cores = 1L)
```

```{r rpt_populate, eval = flag_eval}
for (i in 1:4) {
  ver <- next_version(base_rpt, "2024_11_01")
  slt_rpt$make_new_version_folder(version_name = ver)
}

suppressMessages({
  slt_rpt$mark_best(version_name = "2024_11_01.03",
                    user_entry = list(comment = "Production run"))
  slt_rpt$mark_keep(version_name = "2024_11_01.01",
                    user_entry = list(comment = "Baseline comparison"))
})
```

## Run all reports

```{r rpt_make, eval = flag_eval}
suppressMessages(slt_rpt$make_reports())
print_tree(base_rpt, level = 1)
```

### Key-version report

Current state of every symlink-marked folder.

- Runs automatically when marking/unmarking
- Only tracks symlinks defined in the package registry

```{r rpt_key, eval = flag_eval}
data.table::fread(file.path(base_rpt, "report_key_versions.csv"))[, ..show_vars]
```

### Non-symlinked folders

Folders that exist but have no active symlink — useful for identifying cleanup candidates.

```{r rpt_nonsym, eval = flag_eval}
data.table::fread(file.path(base_rpt, "report_all_logs_non_symlink.csv"))[, ..show_vars]
```

### Discrepancy report

If any versioned logs have unexpected structure (missing fields, extra rows, schema drift), a `REPORT_DISCREPANCIES.csv` file is written.  A clean project produces no discrepancy file.

- Runs automatically when marking/unmarking

```{r rpt_discrep, eval = flag_eval}
try(data.table::fread(file.path(base_rpt, "REPORT_DISCREPANCIES.csv")))
```

```{r rpt_cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = flag_eval}
unlink(base_rpt, recursive = TRUE)
```
